findings.finding: An advertising platform: substantially all revenue is advertising on Facebook/Instagram/WhatsApp/Messenger (Q3 2026 advertising 63.06B of 64.60B revenue); Reality Labs is 0.44B revenue against an 18-19B guided 2026 loss. No customer is 10% of revenue; advertisers have no long-term commitments, so demand is funded by millions of advertisers' budgets and can be cut quickly.

Q3 2026 revenue +26% came from price per ad +14% and impressions +10%; impressions growth has decelerated four quarters running (+18%, +19%, +14%, +10%) while price per ad accelerated (+6%, +12%, +12%, +14%). Users barely grow (DAP 3.64B, +3%); ARPP +23%. Growth is yield/ranking driven (AI recommendation and ad models), not audience growth; by geography US&Canada +33%, Europe +18%, APAC +16%, RoW +34%.

Structural with a macro beta: revenue grew every year 2020-2025 except 2022 (-1.1%, iOS signal loss plus ad recession) and then re-accelerated to +16%, +22%, +22% and about +27% in 2026 (9M actual plus the Q4 guide). Advertising is cyclical in a recession but the business is not a commodity cycle; treated structural, the 2022 drawdown sized in the bear.

Computed mature_growth / stalwart confirmed with a qualification: revenue compounding above 20% at 200B+ scale is fast-grower speed, but the investment phase (capex 135-145B in 2026, about 55% of revenue, FCF negative in Q3) makes it a capital-heavy compounder whose value depends on the return on AI capex, so the lens is FCFF with explicit reinvestment, not a P/E on trailing earnings.

Conservative guider: 7 of 7 quarters beat the revenue guide midpoint, mean actual/midpoint 1.041 (Q3 2026 64.60B vs 61-64B guided, above the top). The Q4 2026 guide 73-76B (+22% to +27%) behaves as a floor, but no automatic beat is assumed beyond the track-record ratio the engine applies to the remainder.

Reported earnings are distorted both ways: Q3 2026 carries a 9.89B attorneys-general settlement charge (EPS 3.83 vs 7.40 ex-charge), Q2 2026 a 2.4B legal charge, Q1 2026 an 8.03B CAMT tax benefit and Q3 2025 a 15.93B tax charge. Legal charges recur as a category (accruals 11.58B current + 8.30B non-current, 5.3B contingent not accrued), so ex-charge earnings are not a legal-cost-free run rate. SBC is a real cost: 21.05B in 9M 2026 (11.6% of revenue vs 10.2% in 2025) and no buybacks in 9M 2026.

ROIC last 28.7% (average 31.4%) but incremental ROIC fell to 14.9%: invested capital roughly doubled from end-2024 to Q3 2026 while TTM revenue rose about 77B, an incremental sales-to-capital of about 0.55 versus about 0.8 over 2021-2024. Operating margin fell from 41.4% (2025) to 20.1% reported / about 35% ex-charge in Q3 2026 as depreciation, cloud capacity and AI token costs ramp.

Non-cancelable commitments 454.5B (121.4B due 2027), leases not yet commenced 355.7B, data-center ventures maximum exposure to loss 68.4B including 41.5B residual value guarantees; 10.8B of restricted cash is escrow, not liquidity. Net debt about 1.2B at Q3 2026 before the raise (cash and securities 82.45B vs debt 83.67B).

The October 2026 raise reverses a decade of buybacks: 12.5B 6.50% mandatory convertible preferred closed 2026-10-29 (converts 2029-08-15 into 17.0-20.0M Class A shares; carried as a claim at its 12.5B liquidation preference, not also as dilution), 40M Class A shares sold forward at 625 (net about 24.9B, settlement at Meta's choice by 2027-11-19: modelled as FY2027 equity proceeds), and a planned about 60B ATM with no agreement, size or timing (a disclosed risk, not modelled). Class C non-voting stock (charter effective 2027-01-19) widens the issuance channel.

Management says it will sustain strong revenue growth through 2027 and that new AI products (Muse agent, business messaging, subscriptions) can add incremental revenue in 2027, while investing aggressively; 2027 expense and capex outlook only at the Q4 call. Delivery evidence so far is in the core ads (ranking-model conversion gains, partnership ads over a 15B run rate, Meta One subscriptions over 15M), not yet in Muse revenue (no numbers given). Reality Labs loss guided to narrow to about 15B in 2027 from 18-19B.

flags: Piotroski 5/8 (mixed): deteriorating cash conversion and margins during the capex ramp
incremental ROIC 14.9% vs ROIC 28.7%: the AI capex earns far less per dollar so far than the legacy base
Q3 2026 free cash flow negative (-2.12B company definition) with capex 34.9B; capex/OCF above 1
Family of Apps segment margin down 22 points y/y in Q3 2026 (charge plus infrastructure costs)
headline earnings distorted: 93% of Q3 reported net income gap is one-off; legal charges recur (2.4B Q2, 9.89B Q3, 5.3B contingent not accrued, youth trials from February 2027)
SBC 11.6% of revenue in 9M 2026 with no buybacks: SBC dilution now offset only by the cash-tax net share settlement
equity raise about 37.5B (12.5B preferred closed, 25B forward) plus a planned about 60B ATM: current holders fund the capex
off-balance exposure: data-center ventures residual value guarantees 41.5B, 355.7B leases not yet commenced
tax volatility: gross unrecognized tax benefits 20.8B; effective rate 87% (Q3 2025), 2% (9M 2026), 24% (Q3 2026)

economics.reason: Advertising demand grew in five of six years since 2020 and re-accelerated after the single down year 2022 (-1.1%, iOS signal loss plus ad recession); price per ad and conversion gains are model-driven. Macro beta is carried in the bear, not by cycle normalization.
